summary: PR C (#2793): full /governance run (Gates 2/3/4/6 -- no C++ touched, so cpp-expert/cpp-safety/quality-engineer not triggered) on docs/user-manual/mcp.md (two new blockquotes under -32007 and -32012) and changelog.d/2793-mcp-customer-manual.fixed.md, reviewed at 8fcc8a7b against origin/dev (0714b75c). 9 agents: security-guardian, docs-writer (Gate 2); architect (Gate 3, sole domain trigger -- docs-only diff); happy-path, unhappy-path, consistency-auditor (Gate 4); compliance-officer, sre, enterprise-readiness (Gate 6). Two forks ran alongside: one traced the exact -32014 vs -32007 mechanism before any prose was written (resolved the issue's own premise as wrong -- the fix belongs under -32007, not the originally-filed -32014, confirmed independently by every agent in this wave including enterprise-readiness's own loop-closure check); one verified the exact reserve()->streamed_reject() why->remediation code mapping after my own re-trace self-contradicted mid-writing (fork-remediation-mismatch). This ledger's rows are transcribed from each agent's full verbatim <result> text, recovered from this session's own raw transcript (task-notification records) after a context compaction had already occurred -- not reconstructed from a compressed summary, and not from memory. No CRITICAL findings from any agent. Two native-severity disagreements are preserved below rather than silently resolved (PP-1: docs-writer HIGH/BLOCKING vs security-guardian+happy-path+sre MEDIUM; GC-1: unhappy-path HIGH (no I/E breakdown given) vs security-guardian+architect+happy-path MEDIUM). consistency-auditor and enterprise-readiness returned no MEDIUM+ findings (enterprise-readiness: PASS, and ran its own loop-closure check confirming the -32007 rescope satisfied #2793's actual acceptance criteria rather than dodging them).

adjudication_rationale: docs-writer derived HIGH/BLOCKING via I4 (harmful operator guidance) blended with I3 (wrong result presented as correct). Re-derived independently against the shared preamble's own I4 definition ("a NAMED action that causes damage"): the bullet's remediation clause is client-side (wait / retry / drop SSE Accept) and is itself accurate regardless of the true cause -- it never names "raise --mcp-max-streams-per-principal" as an action. The harmful inference requires a step the prose itself doesn't state. happy-path explicitly considered and rejected I4 on exactly this ground ("the operator-action chain requires an inference the new prose doesn't itself state, making I4 speculative rather than verified"); security-guardian and sre independently landed the same way. 3 of 4 direct reporters converge on I7/MEDIUM; reclassified to MEDIUM/SHOULD. Fixed regardless of blocking status, in the same fix round as GC-1 (both bullets rewritten together in e1cd257a). severity_native retained verbatim as docs-writer reported it.
trigger: an operator or client author reads the -32012 streamed-POST bullet, concludes --mcp-max-streams-per-principal governs the post_per_principal_cap reject, and raises that flag expecting relief -- concrete, plausible: this is exactly the capacity-planning question the doc exists to answer ahead of the default flip
summary: The first bullet of the new -32012 streamed-POST blockquote stated the cause was "the same --max-sse-streams / --mcp-max-streams-per-principal cap the GET channel draws from above." False for the per-principal half: server/core/src/mcp_server.cpp:6065-6066 passes the compile-time constant mcp::sse_bus::kPerPrincipalMcpPost (stream_budget.hpp:131, = 4, static_assert-tied to kMaxStreamedPostsPerSession, mcp_stream.hpp:166), never the CLI flag's cfg_.mcp_max_streams_per_principal value -- --mcp-max-streams-per-principal is threaded only into the GET channel (mcp_stream.cpp:~699-701). The flag's own --help text says so explicitly (main.cpp:518-524): 'Does NOT govern streamed POST responses, whose per-session allowance is a fixed 4 twinned to the replay ring's pin slots, so a principal's held-open ceiling is this value + 4.' 4 independent reporters, all verified: docs-writer (this row's source; also confirmed the GET-channel text elsewhere in mcp.md is correctly scoped -- this is an isolated new-bullet defect, not a broader pattern), security-guardian (F1), happy-path (Gate-4 finding, Q4), sre (Capacity finding). architect's F1 covers the same bullet's global-cap half (see GC-1) but does not independently re-derive the per-principal-specific falsity, so is not counted toward this row's independent_reporters.

adjudication_rationale: unhappy-path reported severity 'high' in its own YAML vocabulary without the shared preamble's TRIGGER/IMPACT/EXPOSURE breakdown. Re-derived: IMPACT=I7 (doc misdescribes shipped capacity behaviour for a real, reachable subset of cases) -- no HIGH-raise condition applies (not breaking-change / security / data-loss / migration / irreversible-op; the client-side remediation text itself is byte-identical regardless of cause, so no client is misdirected into a different action, only a human reader forming a wrong mental model). EXPOSURE: no applicable modifier. Derives MEDIUM, matching the other 3 reporters' independent derivations exactly. Reclassified to MEDIUM/SHOULD. Fixed via a full restructure into two error.message-scoped groups (e1cd257a) rather than a word-level patch, per unhappy-path's own recommended mitigation. The code-level follow-up unhappy-path also proposed (give reserve()'s internal global_record_cap its own reason label, e.g. post_record_cap) and the doc gap in mcp-server.md's admission table (also named by architect, F1, as pre-existing context) are both out of scope for a docs-only PR -- filed as issue #2918. severity_native retained verbatim as unhappy-path reported it.
trigger: a production server with --mcp-enable-streamed-post on sustains yuzu_mcp_stream_rejects_total{reason="post_global_cap"} / repeated -32012 429s driven by McpStreamBridge::reserve()'s internal records_.size() >= 256 check (fed by ALL progress-tracked calls fleet-wide, not just streamed POST) rather than by --max-sse-streams exhaustion -- verified reachable, not hypothetical
summary: The same first bullet's global-cap clause ("checked before the call is even accepted") is false for a second, unrelated cause sharing the identical post_global_cap reason label: McpStreamBridge::reserve()'s own records_.size() >= cfg_.global_record_cap check (mcp_stream_bridge.cpp:340-341), default 256 (mcp_stream_bridge.hpp:240), hardcoded with NO CLI/env wiring anywhere in the tree (confirmed by repo-wide grep), counting every progress-token-bearing bridge record server-wide (streamed or not) -- fires from INSIDE reserve(), i.e. strictly after the pre-admission StreamBudget lease was already acquired, contradicting the bullet's own 'checked before the call is even accepted' framing. Both post_global_cap call sites emit byte-identical error.data.remediation text ('retry shortly, or retry without an SSE Accept for a plain response') -- confirmed identical, not merely similar, by fork-remediation-mismatch's direct trace of both streamed_reject() call sites (mcp_server.cpp:6079-6087 vs :6178-6185). Only error.message distinguishes them ('Concurrent stream cap reached' vs 'Streamed request capacity reached'), which the original bullet never named as the disambiguator despite promising 'distinguish them by error.data.remediation' -- a promise the fork confirmed is false for this specific pair of causes. docs/mcp-server.md's own admission table (~line 244) has the identical gap pre-existing (no row for the internal record cap) -- not this PR's defect, but this PR layered a new, more specific, equally-wrong causal claim on top of it. 4 independent reporters: unhappy-path (this row's source, no formal I/E breakdown given -- reported 'severity: high' directly in its own YAML vocabulary), security-guardian (F2, MEDIUM/I7), architect (F1, MEDIUM/I7), happy-path (same Q4 finding as PP-1, global-cap clause specifically, MEDIUM).

adjudication_rationale: Two agents examined the identical fact and derived different bands: architect I7/MEDIUM (the header positively misstates a shipped, flag-independent mechanism as flag-gated), security-guardian I8/LOW (the remediation and the quoted error string are both correct regardless, so a reader who greps their actual error still lands on the right section). Sided with architect's I7: the shared preamble defines I8 as 'degraded but correct -- slow, wasteful, noisy; output still right', which describes a functioning-but-suboptimal mechanism, not a doc header that misattributes a mechanism's trigger condition to the wrong flag -- that is a doc-truth gap (I7) even though the practical harm is bounded by the string-match safety net security-guardian correctly identified. MEDIUM/SHOULD. Fixed by rewriting the header/framing in e1cd257a to state the mechanism is reachable today independent of the flag, with the flag adding only a second, faster route to the same state.
trigger: a GET-channel progress consumer resuming with a Last-Event-ID that has aged out of the replay ring under the shipped 3a default (--mcp-enable-streamed-post OFF) -- verified reachable without any opt-in flag
summary: The new -32007 blockquote's header, 'A live session can also end up here (streamed POST, --mcp-enable-streamed-post)', scoped the entire kGap -> session-termination -> -32007 consequence as conditional on that off-by-default flag. Verified false: AttachStatus::kGap -> sessions.terminate() (mcp_stream.cpp:1659-1676) is reached from the GET /mcp/v1/ handler unconditionally, gated only by streaming_on (--mcp-no-streaming, default OFF i.e. Streamable HTTP is ON by default) -- never by --mcp-enable-streamed-post. The 3a progress bridge is explicitly 'Shipped' per docs/mcp-server.md:180-187 and publishes unpinned frames into the same ring (mcp_stream_bridge.cpp:1642-1644), subject to the same 500-frame/64KiB eviction as any other frame -- no pin, no bridge, no streamed POST involved at all. A GET-channel client that simply falls behind (network blip, slow reconnect, long high-frequency execution) hits the identical outcome today, with the flag off. 2 independent reporters: architect (this row's source, MEDIUM/I7 -- 'doc absent for shipped behaviour, 3a is explicitly Shipped'), security-guardian (F3, LOW/I8 -- 'remediation given is correct regardless of root cause, so degraded-but-correct not actively harmful'). Both verified the same underlying fact; they differ only on whether the header's scoping error itself, versus its harmlessness to the reader who greps the literal error string, is the controlling fact.

trigger: a reader takes the -32007 blockquote's phrasing literally in isolation
summary: 'Repeated client disconnects on one session can trigger the admission reclaim' compresses the actual trigger: disconnects alone never trigger the reclaim -- a SUBSEQUENT streamed-POST reserve() call hitting the per-session pin/charge cap does (selection only runs inside reserve(), mcp_stream_bridge.cpp:342-427). docs/mcp-server.md's own cited source describes it correctly ('Admission now reclaims a slot first ... and the new call is admitted' -- an admission-time event, not a disconnect-time one). Remediation is identical either way (re-initialize; fetch by execution_id), so no operator action turns on the distinction -- both reporters independently capped this at LOW/I8 rather than I4 for exactly that reason. 2 independent reporters: docs-writer (this row's source), unhappy-path (2nd finding, same gap, same LOW severity).

summary: While consolidating the 9 agents' findings, independently discovered (not flagged by any of the 9 agents) that the internal metric_reason/post_* strings (post_per_principal_cap, post_global_cap, post_pin_slots) passed to streamed_reject() are used ONLY for a Prometheus counter label and an audit-log detail string -- they are NEVER part of the client-facing wire response. error_response_a4/error_response_null_a4 (mcp_jsonrpc.hpp:250-279) emit only correlation_id/retry_after_ms/remediation in error.data; no reason field exists on the wire. Re-checked my own already-committed prose against this fact: it never named these internal strings as if client-visible (it always spoke in terms of error.message and error.data.remediation, the actual wire-visible signals), so no separate fix was required for this specific issue -- but the discovery confirmed the restructuring approach (organize the -32012 rewrite by error.message, the real client-visible discriminator, rather than by the internal reason label) was correct, and architect's independent Finding 1 (RS-1/GC-1's sibling) reached the same architectural conclusion from a different angle.

Before pushing the e1cd257a fix round, called advisor() per this session's own established pattern (fix rounds have twice shipped new defects of the class they closed on this branch family, per memory feedback-fix-rounds-ship-new-defects). advisor() caught two precision regressions introduced BY the fix round itself, both verified against mcp_server.cpp / stream_budget.hpp before fixing (rows REM-1, SCOPE-1 below), and correctly assessed no action was needed on ledger-writing timing (this ledger) since the verbatim agent reports were still fully recoverable from the raw session transcript at write time, despite an intervening compaction -- recovered via task-notification records rather than reconstructed from the compacted summary.

trigger: a reader receiving a post_per_principal_cap 429 tries to map error.data.remediation's exact wording back to which of the two pre-admission causes fired, using the doc's own promised structure
summary: The e1cd257a rewrite fixing PP-1/GC-1 collapsed the two pre-admission causes' remediation into one combined line ('Remediation for either: wait for one of your streamed calls to finish, or retry shortly, or resend...'), losing the per-cause mapping the original (pre-PR) wire text actually carries. Verified against mcp_server.cpp:6079-6087: the remediation string genuinely differs by cause -- per_principal ? "wait for one of your streamed calls to finish, ..." : "retry shortly, ...". Losing that mapping is exactly the class of defect this fix round was closing elsewhere (GC-1's whole point was that error.message, and by extension the per-cause remediation text, is the real discriminator -- this regression quietly discarded the one piece of that discriminator a reader could actually use for the per-principal-vs-global split). Caught by advisor(), not any of the 9 governance agents (all 9 reviewed the ORIGINAL, pre-fix bullet, which did not yet have this combined-line structure -- the regression was introduced by my own fix, after the wave completed).

trigger: a reader with concurrent multi-session activity as the same principal tries to reason about why they hit post_per_principal_cap while any single one of their sessions is nowhere near its own pin-slot cap
summary: The e1cd257a rewrite's per-principal bullet said the fixed-4 cap is 'twinned to the replay ring's per-session pin-slot count', which reads as though the two caps share a scope. They don't: kPerPrincipalMcpPost (stream_budget.hpp:131) is checked via StreamBudget keyed by (surface, principal) (stream_budget.hpp:189-197, confirmed independently by sre's own capacity-lens read of the same lines) -- summed across every session that principal holds open. The pin-slot cap in the next checkpoint is keyed by SESSION. Both happen to equal 4 (enforced equal by a static_assert), but a principal with multiple concurrent sessions can exhaust the per-principal cap while any single one of those sessions' own pin slots are nowhere near full -- 'twinned to' conflates a numeric coincidence with a scope identity. Caught by advisor(), not any of the 9 governance agents (none examined the per-principal cap's cross-session summation behaviour specifically; sre came closest by citing the exact (surface, principal) keying but did not flag the 'twinned to' phrase's scope implication).
